questions.def: 'Not until X that Y' needs 'later' to refer to a point in time.
questions.question: It was not until ___ that she realised her mistake.

questions.def: 'Only then' inverts subject-verb for emphasis in formal writing.
questions.question: Only ___ did I understand the true meaning of the poem.

questions.def: Negative adverbials invert subject-verb: 'on no account should you deny'.
questions.question: On no account ___ access to confidential information.

questions.def: 'Only when' requires inversion and adds emphasis.
questions.question: ___ I finish this report, I can finally relax.

questions.def: 'Not only...but also' is a correlative conjunction for emphasis.
questions.question: Not ___ did he offer an apology, but he also sent flowers.

questions.def: 'Little' (meaning almost nothing) requires inversion for emphasis.
questions.question: Little ___ that I was making a mistake.

questions.def: 'So + adjective' causes subject-verb inversion for emphasis.
questions.question: ___ was the performance that everyone applauded enthusiastically.

questions.def: 'Given' introduces a known fact, emphasizing the result.
questions.question: ___ the severity of the situation, we had to act quickly.

questions.def: 'Not until' requires subject-verb inversion in the main clause.
questions.question: Not until later ___ the full extent of the damage.

questions.def: 'No sooner...than' expresses immediate succession, emphasizing timing.
questions.question: ___ had I sat down than the phone rang.

questions.def: 'Regardless of' emphasizes that the event is unaffected.
questions.question: ___ the rain, the event will proceed as planned.

questions.def: 'Only then' necessitates inversion of the auxiliary verb and subject.
questions.question: Only then ___ the enormity of the task.

questions.def: 'Come what may' emphasizes the speaker's unwavering resolve.
questions.question: ___ be it, I refuse to comply.

questions.def: 'All things considered' emphasizes a comprehensive evaluation.
questions.question: ___, the project was a resounding success.

questions.def: When starting with 'never', inversion is required (auxiliary + subject).
questions.question: Never ___ such a breathtaking view.

questions.def: 'Much as' expresses a contrast, emphasizing the reservation.
questions.question: ___ I support the proposal, I have some reservations.

questions.def: 'Notwithstanding' emphasizes the contrast between difficulty and perseverance.
questions.question: ___ the difficulties, they persevered.

questions.def: 'Little' at the beginning of the sentence causes subject-verb inversion.
questions.question: Little ___ to be treated with such disrespect.

questions.def: 'Should that' introduces a hypothetical situation with emphasis.
questions.question: ___ be the case, we must proceed cautiously.

questions.def: 'Be that as it may' acknowledges a point but emphasizes the conclusion.
questions.question: ___ as it may, the decision is final.

questions.def: Beginning with 'Never' triggers subject-auxiliary verb inversion for focus.
questions.question: Never ___ to see him again.

questions.def: 'For all' emphasizes the contrast between effort and outcome.
questions.question: ___ the government's efforts, the problem persists.

questions.def: 'Despite' emphasizes the policy's implementation against opposition.
questions.question: ___ the public outcry, the policy was implemented.

questions.def: Only 'later' fits grammatically, indicating a point in time.
questions.question: It wasn't until ___ that I understood the problem.

questions.def: 'However + adjective' introduces a contrasting clause.
questions.question: ___ he may be, he is still my responsibility.

questions.def: Past simple is best: definite point of emphasis in the past.
questions.question: What I ___ was the importance of research.

questions.def: 'Little' triggers subject-verb inversion using 'did'.
questions.question: Little ___ he know the danger he was in.

questions.def: Cleft sentence uses 'it was + pronoun (objective)' for emphasis.
questions.question: It ___ that I saw him, not John.

questions.def: 'Overstress' implies emphasizing something to an excessive degree.
questions.question: I cannot ___ the importance of this enough.

questions.def: 'Come what may' is a fixed expression showing strong resolve.
questions.question: ___ may come, I will stand by you.
